test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following represents the longitudinal extent of India?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**68°7'E and 97°25'E**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **longitudinal extent** of India ranges from **68°7'E to 97°25'E**.
 
• This longitudinal range spans approximately **29° in length**.
 
• The longitudinal extent determines the **time zone** of India, which is calculated based on the 82°30'E longitude (Indian Standard Time or IST).
 
• India's longitudinal extent plays a crucial role in influencing **sunrise and sunset timings** across different parts of the country.
 
• The longitudinal spread contributes to the country's **diverse climatic zones**, with eastern and western parts experiencing slight differences in weather patterns.
 
• The easternmost point of India is **near Kibithu, Arunachal Pradesh**, while the westernmost point is **near Guhar Moti, Gujarat**.
 
• India’s longitudinal extent facilitates **trade and connectivity** with neighboring countries, especially to the east and west.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Incorrect Options**__

 
 
• 56°7'E and 87°25'E: This range does not match the actual longitudinal extent of India. The values are smaller and do not encompass the eastern and western limits of the country.
 
• 58°7'E and 94°25'E: These values are incorrect as they fail to cover India's full longitudinal range.
 
• 54°7'E and 77°25'E: This range is too narrow and does not represent the true longitudinal extent of India.
